components.label: Book shopper
components.responsibility: Own saved search settings and display effective versions.

components.label: Saved-search alerts
components.responsibility: Accept searches and produce bounded daily notification intent.

components.label: Preferences and consent
components.responsibility: Own search versions, timezone and current consent.

components.label: Publication index
components.responsibility: Own committed listing revisions and stable publication sequence.

components.label: Scheduled snapshot matcher
components.responsibility: Scan a fixed committed publication interval, page by total cursor, then commit progress with match writes.

components.label: Change-driven matcher
components.responsibility: Route committed listing events through candidate predicates then exact evaluation.

components.label: Publication change log
components.responsibility: Retain committed publication events and replay positions; support outbox or CDC handoff.

components.label: Unique matches store
components.responsibility: Persist search-version/listing matches with a uniqueness constraint.

components.label: Calendar cutoff planner
components.responsibility: Resolve recipient local dates into explicit UTC half-open intervals, including DST changes.

components.label: Digest materializer
components.responsibility: Freeze recipients, sorted listing identities and payload hash once per period.

components.label: Digest outbox
components.responsibility: Commit digest payload, retry state and uncertain outcomes durably.

components.label: Consent-aware dispatcher
components.responsibility: Recheck consent, claim a fenced attempt, send with stable identity and reconcile ambiguous results.

components.label: Email provider
components.responsibility: Accept or reject mail; only promise idempotency if the selected provider explicitly supports it.

components.label: Delivery feedback consumer
components.responsibility: Verify feedback, deduplicate events and persist delivery or suppression without confusing acceptance with inbox receipt.

components.label: Progress reconciler
components.responsibility: Compare scan/log checkpoints and retained source history; backfill before retention expires.

request.periodId: recipient local date and zone rule

requirements.text: Match newly published listings against versioned saved search predicates without omissions at scan boundaries.
Build one immutable digest per recipient and local calendar period, deduplicating listing matches.
Retry boundedly while distinguishing pending, accepted, delivered, suppressed and uncertain outcomes.
Apply unsubscribe and address suppression at dispatch time, not just when matching.

problem.scope: Book shoppers save searches and receive daily digests for newly published matching listings. Compare scheduled index scans with change-driven matching. Search semantics, consent, timezone cutoffs and uncertain email acceptance are explicit; exactly-once inbox delivery is not promised.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Snapshot boundaries and concurrent transactional updates.
references.title: PostgreSQL transaction isolation

references.supports: Sending acceptance differs from delivery, bounce, complaint and suppression.
references.title: Amazon SES sending events

acceptanceCases.given: A listing commits while an existing scan is paging and a saved predicate is edited.
acceptanceCases.then: No committed listing is skipped; each match names the exact search version and scan boundary.
acceptanceCases.when: Finish the fixed upper-cursor scan and start the next interval.

acceptanceCases.given: The same listing event or scan page is delivered twice.
acceptanceCases.then: The unique match key produces one record per search version/listing; progress cannot outrun committed writes.
acceptanceCases.when: Commit matches and retry after a simulated checkpoint-write interruption.

acceptanceCases.given: A digest is frozen before another matching listing arrives and the local day crosses DST.
acceptanceCases.then: The first payload hash is unchanged; the new listing follows the recorded late-arrival policy, with no invented 24-hour day assumption.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry materialization and then process the following local date.

acceptanceCases.given: A digest is queued and consent is revoked before dispatch authorization.
acceptanceCases.then: Suppress it; a race after provider acceptance is documented as unable to recall already sent mail.

acceptanceCases.given: A provider accepts a digest but its response is lost.
acceptanceCases.then: Keep outcome uncertain until reconciled; retries follow the declared remote idempotency or duplicate-versus-loss policy.

guarantees: Repeated source delivery cannot duplicate a match; a fixed upper cursor prevents a moving pagination boundary.
Provider acceptance and delivery are different states; a stable local ID alone cannot deduplicate a remote side effect.

apis.errors: 403 wrong owner; 409 stale version; 422 invalid predicate
400 invalid token; repeated requests idempotently succeed

assumptions: Published revisions have immutable identities and a committed ordering cursor.
Email acceptance can be uncertain; without provider deduplication, retry may duplicate or fail to deliver.
solutions.chooseWhen: Daily latency is acceptable and an indexed listing store can scan fixed publication intervals.

stages.explanation: Start with a shopper and one alerts boundary; record exact predicates and a daily delivery promise. A saved search has an owner, version, timezone and explicit matching semantics. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters.
invariants: A saved search has an owner, version, timezone and explicit matching semantics.
stages.question: What is a new matching listing?
stages.reason: Start with a shopper and one alerts boundary; record exact predicates and a daily delivery promise.
stages.title: Define search and notification intent

stages.explanation: Expand into authoritative preferences and listing history; do not treat an edited predicate as the old search version. Never mutate an old search version used by an already frozen digest. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters.
invariants: Never mutate an old search version used by an already frozen digest.
stages.question: Which state changes when a shopper edits a search?
stages.reason: Expand into authoritative preferences and listing history; do not treat an edited predicate as the old search version.
stages.title: Separate preferences from publications

stages.explanation: Freeze the upper publication cursor and use keyset pagination inside that interval. Progress never advances past work whose match writes are not durably committed. [A cursor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursor_%28databases%29) records where a query should continue. Its ordering fields must distinguish equal values, and its validity depends on the query and access permissions. Consider this case: A listing commits while an existing scan is paging and a saved predicate is edited.
invariants: Progress never advances past work whose match writes are not durably committed.
stages.question: How do listings become candidate matches?
stages.reason: Freeze the upper publication cursor and use keyset pagination inside that interval.
stages.title: Introduce fixed-window scheduled scans

stages.explanation: Separate candidate discovery from durable exact-match admission with a unique search-version/listing key. An edited search version is a distinct matching policy; historic digests keep their original content. [A search index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_engine_indexing) maps query terms to candidate records. The interface must still associate each response with the active query and preserve the user’s chosen filters.
invariants: An edited search version is a distinct matching policy; historic digests keep their original content.
stages.question: What if a scan or event is repeated?
stages.reason: Separate candidate discovery from durable exact-match admission with a unique search-version/listing key.
stages.title: Persist unique search/listing matches

stages.explanation: Add a calendar cutoff and materializer; immutable recipient/period digests pin a publication watermark and payload hash. DST days may contain 23 or 25 hours; period identity is a local date with a resolved UTC interval. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.
invariants: DST days may contain 23 or 25 hours; period identity is a local date with a resolved UTC interval.
stages.question: What does daily mean across timezone changes?
stages.reason: Add a calendar cutoff and materializer; immutable recipient/period digests pin a publication watermark and payload hash.
stages.title: Freeze local-day digest contents

stages.explanation: Add an independent dispatcher and provider; check current suppression before claiming an attempt. A dispatch authorization defines the unsubscribe cutoff; an already accepted email cannot be recalled. [Access control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_control) decides whether an authenticated identity may perform a particular action. The check must apply to the actual resource and operation, including cached and asynchronous paths.
invariants: A dispatch authorization defines the unsubscribe cutoff; an already accepted email cannot be recalled.
stages.question: Can a queued digest ignore a later unsubscribe?
stages.reason: Add an independent dispatcher and provider; check current suppression before claiming an attempt.
stages.title: Dispatch with current consent

stages.explanation: Separate accepted, delivered, bounce and complaint receipts; preserve an uncertain state after a lost response. Do not claim exactly-once inbox delivery from a unique local outbox row. [Change data capture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change_data_capture) turns committed data changes into an ordered stream for other components. Consumers still need replay positions and duplicate handling when delivery is retried.
invariants: Do not claim exactly-once inbox delivery from a unique local outbox row.
stages.question: Does a successful send mean the message arrived?
stages.reason: Separate accepted, delivered, bounce and complaint receipts; preserve an uncertain state after a lost response.
stages.title: Record provider feedback and ambiguity

stages.explanation: Compare durable checkpoints with retained publication history and run a bounded overlap backfill. If retention was exceeded, report the uncovered interval and rebuild; do not silently claim complete coverage. [A checkpoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkpointing) records enough progress to restart without repeating everything. Its usefulness depends on which state is durable and whether later effects can be replayed safely.
invariants: If retention was exceeded, report the uncovered interval and rebuild; do not silently claim complete coverage.
stages.question: What if the worker loses progress or source history expires?
stages.reason: Compare durable checkpoints with retained publication history and run a bounded overlap backfill.
stages.title: Reconcile interrupted progress

solutions.title: Scheduled publication scans and daily digests
tradeoffs: Search-by-search scans repeat work and create scheduled load peaks.
Fixed cursor boundaries and retained history are necessary to avoid missing late work.
